# Graphical Playground

> An interactive, browser-based platform where students deconstruct and rebuild graphics-engine systems from the ground up, from raw Vulkan commands to full render pipelines. Explore creative coding, canvas experiments, and real-time graphics programming.

Graphical Playground (GP) is an open-source C++23 game engine and educational platform, pairing a high-performance cross-platform engine (Windows, Linux, macOS, iOS, Android, WASM) with a cloud-native e-learning curriculum covering Vulkan, DirectX 11/12, OpenGL/OpenGL ES, GLSL, HLSL, and real-time rendering pipelines.

## Docs

- [Documentation](https://docs.graphical-playground.com): Engine architecture, API reference, build system (GPBT), and curriculum guides.
- [GitHub Organization](https://github.com/GraphicalPlayground): Source code, issue tracker, and contribution guidelines.

## Product

- [Products](https://graphical-playground.com/products): Overview of the engine and learning platform offerings.
    - [GPlayd Engine](https://graphical-playground.com/products/engine): High-performance, cross-platform graphics engine.
    - [GPlayd Cloud](https://graphical-playground.com/products/cloud): Cloud-native learning platform for graphics programming.
    - [GPlayd Studio](https://graphical-playground.com/products/studio): Integrated development environment for graphics projects.
- [Features](https://graphical-playground.com/features): Overview of the engine and learning platform capabilities.
- [Pricing](https://graphical-playground.com/pricing): Plans for individuals, students, and institutions.
- [Changelog](https://graphical-playground.com/changelog): Release notes and engine updates.
